SECTION VIII - ANY IRREVERSIBLE AND IRRETRIEVABLE COMMITMENTS OF RESOURCES WHICH WOULD BE INVOLVED IN THE PROPOSED ACTION SHOULD IT BE IMPLEMENTED
8.01 The installation of the powerhouse and all supporting facilities will require an extensive bill of materials commonly utilized in construction including gravel, sand, cement, copper, steel, lumber, and others. To a considerable degree, these basic materials are reclaimable with some penalty; however, their commitment to the project should generally be considered a long-term and irreversible commitment of resources.
8.02 In addition to the required industrial resource, the project will involve a substantial expenditure of manpower, capital, and energy which will constitute a significant commitment of resources.
8.03 The project will also require a minimal commitment of land as a basic resource. This land is necessarily lost for the life of the project so far as other productive uses are concerned. The regulated streamflows of the Rio Grande from Amistad to Falcon Reservoir will be slightly modified as a result of hydroelectric operation. Theoretically, this would not be an irreversible situation.
